expectation: `orderedDestinationGroups` passes the `Map` returned by `groupByDestination` to `orderManifestGroups`, whose comparator reads a `destination` field that the `[key, group]` entries lack, so the groups keep insertion order instead of ascending lexical order.
finding: In `src/dispatch/manifest.mjs:42`, `orderedDestinationGroups` passes the `Map` returned by `groupByDestination(records)` (`lines 3-9`) directly to `orderManifestGroups` (`line 11`), which spreads `[...groups]` into `[key, records]` tuples where `.destination` is `undefined`, leaving the groups unsorted in insertion order.

requirementSource.requirement: `orderedDestinationGroups` returns the destination groups of the records in ascending lexical order.

expectation: The geocoder contract defines `geocoder.lookup` only for known addresses, so it cannot be established whether an unknown address resolves to `undefined` (left out), resolves to another value (kept) or rejects (the whole call rejects).
finding: In `src/dispatch/queue.mjs:34`, `locateStops` filters on `stop.point !== undefined` after `await geocoder.lookup(stop.address)`. However, `docs/dispatch/adapter-contracts.md:3` defines `geocoder.lookup(address)` only for known addresses and does not specify whether unknown addresses resolve to `undefined`, resolve to `null`, or reject, so behavior for unknown addresses cannot be established.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/adapter-contracts.md`, `locateStops` leaves out every stop whose address the geocoder does not know.

expectation: `withinVehicleCapacity` converts the limit to grams and requires the clamped remainder to be above zero, so a total equal to the limit (remainder 0) is rejected.
finding: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md` rules 28-29 (`lines 58-59`), package weights are in grams and vehicle limits are in kilograms. When `weight === limit * 1000` (equal to the configured limit), `remainingVehicleCapacity(limit * 1000, weight)` (`src/dispatch/capacity.mjs:12`) returns `0`, and `withinVehicleCapacity` (`line 3`) checks `> 0`, returning `false`.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, `withinVehicleCapacity` accepts a total equal to the configured limit.

expectation: `canPlanRoute` checks `routes:admin` in the actor's own scopes instead of its held scopes, so an admin scope held through an active claim does not meet the ownership requirement.
finding: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md` rules 3-4 (`lines 9-10`), held scopes include active claims as well as `actor.scopes`, and holding `routes:admin` meets depot ownership for every depot. In `src/dispatch/access.mjs:3`, `canPlanRoute` checks `actor.scopes.includes('routes:admin')` instead of `effectiveScopes(actor, now).includes('routes:admin')`, rejecting actors who hold `routes:admin` via an active claim.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, `canPlanRoute` treats an actor holding `routes:admin` as owning every depot.

expectation: `effectiveScopes` drops only the actor's own scopes when it is suspended and still adds active-claim scopes, so a suspended actor with an active `routes:plan` claim can plan.
finding: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md` line 3 and rule 5 (`line 11`, overriding rule 4 `line 10`), a suspended actor has no held scopes. In `src/dispatch/access.mjs:5`, `effectiveScopes` still includes active claim scopes when `actor.suspended === true` (and `line 3` still checks `actor.scopes.includes('routes:admin')`), permitting a suspended actor with an active `'routes:plan'` claim to pass `canPlanRoute`.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, `canPlanRoute` refuses every suspended actor.

expectation: `handleAnnouncementFailure` removes the copy returned by `store.get`, and `store.remove` removes only the exact stored object, so the stored manifest is not removed.
finding: Under `docs/dispatch/storage-contract.md:6-7`, `store.get(id)` resolves to a new copy of the stored manifest, whereas `store.remove(manifest)` removes a stored manifest only when given the exact stored object. In `src/dispatch/publisher.mjs:10-13` and `src/dispatch/manifest.mjs:32`, `handleAnnouncementFailure` passes the copy returned by `store.get(manifest.id)` to `store.remove(current)`, so the stored manifest is not removed when announcement delivery fails.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/storage-contract.md`, `publishWithAnnouncement` removes the stored manifest when announcement delivery fails.

expectation: `stripCredentials` recurses only into values whose constructor is `Object`, so credentials inside arrays below `auth` are kept.
finding: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md` rules 23-24 (`lines 47-48`), fields named `token`, `secret`, or `password` must be removed at every depth of the redacted value. In `src/dispatch/telemetry.mjs:7,13-14`, `stripCredentials` only recurses when `value?.constructor === Object`, leaving credentials inside arrays (such as `event.auth = {grants: [{token: 'secret'}]}`) or null-prototype objects under `auth` unredacted (and ignoring `auth` fields nested deeper in `event`).

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, `redactManifestEvent` removes every credential nested below an `auth` field.

expectation: `buildManifest` copies each record shallowly and `labelDriver` assigns the label onto the supplied driver object, so supplied records are mutated.
finding: In `src/dispatch/manifest.mjs:26,34`, `buildManifest` copies each top-level record with `{...record, ...}` but `labelDriver` executes `Object.assign(driver, {label: preserveManifestDriver(driver.label)})` on `record.driver`, mutating `driver.label` on the caller's supplied record object in place.

requirementSource.requirement: `buildManifest` copies record objects instead of mutating supplied records.

expectation: `publishManifest` maps entries through an async callback, and every resulting promise is truthy, so a manifest with invalid entries is stored.
finding: In `src/dispatch/publisher.mjs:5-6`, `publishManifest` creates `checks` using an `async` callback (`manifest.entries.map(async entry => manifestEntryIsValid(entry))`), producing an array of truthy `Promise` instances, so `checks.every(Boolean)` always evaluates to `true` and invalid entries are still stored via `stageManifest`.

requirementSource.requirement: `publishManifest` stores the manifest only when every entry is valid.

expectation: `asPublicationError` marks a failure transient when it has a finite `retryAfter` even if it is marked `transient: false`, so `publishWithRetry` retries a failure rule 27 makes non-transient.
finding: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md` line 3 and rule 27 (`line 54`, overriding rule 26 `line 53`), a failure marked `transient: false` is never transient even if it carries a finite numeric `retryAfter`. In `src/dispatch/publisher.mjs:19`, `asPublicationError` computes `transient: error?.transient === true || Number.isFinite(error?.retryAfter)`, causing `publishWithRetry` to retry failures marked `transient: false` when `retryAfter` is finite.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, `publishWithRetry` retries only failures that the Failure classification rules make transient.

expectation: The public dispatch entry omits the executor surface.
finding: Public dispatch entry `src/dispatch/index.mjs` (`lines 1-11`) re-exports planning, manifest, publication, storage, serialization, and telemetry modules, but omits `./executor.mjs` (and `./runtime.mjs`), leaving execution operations (`executeAuthorizedPlan`, `executeDryRun`, `planFailure`, `runEligibleStops`, `emitPlanCreated`, `pendingStops`, and `dispatchRoute`) disconnected from the public entry.

expectation: `coalesceAcrossGroups` records raw package IDs but filters normalized IDs, so a duplicate that differs only in surrounding whitespace survives in a later group.
finding: In `src/dispatch/manifest.mjs:36-40`, `coalesceAcrossGroups` checks normalized (trimmed) package IDs against `seen` (`line 37`) but adds the unnormalized `group.packageIds` entries to `seen` (`line 38`), so duplicate IDs that require trimming or string coercion (such as `' P1 '` followed by `'P1'`) are not removed across groups.

requirementSource.requirement: `coalescePackages` removes duplicate package IDs across the complete manifest.

expectation: `nextRetryDelay` tests `retryAfter` by truthiness, so a server-provided `retryAfter` of 0 falls back to the computed backoff instead of a 0 ms delay.
finding: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md` rules 6-8 (`lines 15-17`), a finite numeric `retryAfter` in seconds replaces computed backoff (capped at 2000 ms). In `src/dispatch/retry.mjs:24`, `nextRetryDelay` tests truthiness (`retryAfter ? ...`), so a valid `retryAfter` of `0` falls back to `computeBackoff(attempt)` instead of returning `0`, while truthy non-finite or non-numeric `retryAfter` values bypass `computeBackoff`.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, `nextRetryDelay` applies the Retry timing rules to every server-provided `retryAfter`.

expectation: `executeAuthorizedPlan` awaits dispatch as an argument of `unlessForbidden`, so dispatch runs before the authorization result is applied.
finding: In `src/dispatch/executor.mjs:4`, `executeAuthorizedPlan` evaluates `await dispatchRoute(dispatch, route)` as an argument before calling `unlessForbidden(...)`, invoking `dispatch(route)` (`src/dispatch/runtime.mjs:5`) even when `canPlanRoute(actor, route, now)` is `false`.

expectation: `stopsForDriver` compares each stop's own `driver`, so a stop with a `reassignment` is returned for its original driver and not for the driver of its `reassignment`, which rule 30 makes its assigned driver.
finding: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md` rule 30 (`line 63`), a stop's assigned driver is `stop.reassignment.driver` when the stop has a `reassignment`, and otherwise `stop.driver`. requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, `chooseDeparture` applies every Departure timing rule.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, the next dispatch time is the later supplied bound adjusted by Departure timing rules 10, 12, and 13.

expectation: Plan-created telemetry depends on when the store invokes `onCommit`, which no available contract defines.
finding: Repeated from `.scratch/0001-dispatch-control/issues/01-assemble-dispatch-plan.md:28`: `emitPlanCreated` (`src/dispatch/executor.mjs:14-17`) and `savePlan` (`src/dispatch/storage.mjs:1-5`) pass `onStored` as `{onCommit: onStored}` to `store.write`, whose contract is not defined in `docs/dispatch/storage-contract.md` (`lines 11-15`) or elsewhere in the repository, so whether `plan.created` is emitted only after storage succeeds cannot be established.

requirementSource.requirement: Plan-created telemetry is emitted only after plan storage succeeds.

expectation: The stop comparator coerces a text `sequence` such as `'2'` to a number, so a stop without a finite numeric sequence does not follow the equal-priority stops that have one.
finding: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md` rule 18 (`line 33`), a stop without a finite numeric `sequence` must follow every stop of equal priority that has one. In `src/dispatch/queue.mjs:6,8`, `compareStops` uses `(left.sequence ?? Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER) - (right.sequence ?? Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER)`, which fails to treat non-nullish non-finite values (`''`, `false`, `'abc'`, `NaN`, `-Infinity`, `Infinity`) as missing a finite numeric sequence (for example placing `sequence: ''` before `sequence: 1`) and also orders finite sequences above `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` after `undefined`.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, the ordinary stop-ordering operation follows the Stop priority rules.

expectation: `authorizeRouteBatch` accepts the batch when `findIndex` returns 0, so a batch whose first route fails depot ownership is authorized.
finding: In `src/dispatch/access.mjs:7-10`, `authorizeRouteBatch` returns `firstRejected <= 0` instead of `firstRejected < 0` (`firstRejected === -1`). When the first route in the batch (`index 0`) fails `requireDepotOwner` (`line 14`), `findIndex` returns `0` and `authorizeRouteBatch` returns `true` instead of rejecting the batch.

requirementSource.requirement: Batch authorization rejects the batch when any route fails depot ownership.

expectation: The weighing contract does not state the unit of the weight that `scale.read` resolves to, so it cannot be established that weighed package weights are in grams.
finding: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md` rule 28 (`line 58`), recorded package weights must be in grams, and `weighPackages` (`src/dispatch/capacity.mjs:20`) stores `await scale.read(entry.packageId)` directly. However, `docs/dispatch/adapter-contracts.md:8` states only that `scale.read(packageId)` resolves to the measured weight without specifying its unit, so whether recorded weights are in grams cannot be established.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, package weighing records each package weight in the unit that the Vehicle capacity rules give.

expectation: Arguments are evaluated before `unlessForbidden` runs, so authorized execution invokes dispatch before it can reject the caller.
finding: Repeated from `.scratch/0001-dispatch-control/issues/01-assemble-dispatch-plan.md:20`: in `src/dispatch/executor.mjs:4`, `executeAuthorizedPlan` eagerly awaits `dispatchRoute(dispatch, route)` (`src/dispatch/runtime.mjs:5`) before `unlessForbidden` checks `canPlanRoute`, invoking `dispatch` even for unauthorized callers.

requirementSource.requirement: Authorized execution rejects a caller before invoking dispatch.

expectation: Retry-count parsing accepts any text that `Number` converts to an integer from 0 through 3, including text that is not base-10 digits such as `'0x2'`.
finding: Repeated from `.scratch/0001-dispatch-control/issues/01-assemble-dispatch-plan.md:30`: under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md` rules 21-22 (`lines 42-43`), `parseRetryCount` in `src/dispatch/retry.mjs:3-6` uses `Number(value)` and accepts invalid inputs such as `""`, `" 1 "`, `"0x2"`, `"1.0"`, `null`, `false`, `true`, and `[]` instead of rejecting every non-conforming value.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, retry-count parsing accepts exactly the valid retry counts and rejects every other value.

expectation: A failure marked `transient: false` that carries a finite `retryAfter` is rewrapped as transient, so publication retries do not stop for it.
finding: Repeated from `.scratch/0001-dispatch-control/issues/02-publish-dispatch-manifest.md:46`: under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md` line 3 and rule 27 (`line 54`), a failure marked `transient: false` is never transient, yet `asPublicationError` (`src/dispatch/publisher.mjs:19`) marks `{transient: false, retryAfter: 1}` as `transient: true`, so `publishWithRetry` retries instead of stopping immediately.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, publication retries stop immediately for failures that the Failure classification rules do not make transient.

expectation: A suspended actor keeps the scopes of its active claims in `effectiveScopes`, so `canPlanRoute` can still allow it.
finding: Repeated from `.scratch/0001-dispatch-control/issues/01-assemble-dispatch-plan.md:51`: under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md` line 3 and rule 5 (`line 11`), a suspended actor has no held scopes, but `effectiveScopes` (`src/dispatch/access.mjs:5`) retains active claims when `actor.suspended === true` (and `canPlanRoute` `line 3` checks `actor.scopes.includes('routes:admin')`), allowing a suspended actor with an active `'routes:plan'` claim to plan routes.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, a suspended actor cannot plan any route.

expectation: Delivery notices are sent to the raw `phone`, so an entry whose `phone` contains spaces or hyphens is not notified at its contact phone (rule 33).
finding: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md` rule 33 (`line 66`), an entry's contact phone is its `phone` with every space (` `) and hyphen (`-`) character removed. In `src/dispatch/publisher.mjs:31`, `sendDeliveryNotices` passes raw `entry.phone` directly to `sms.send` without removing spaces and hyphens.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, delivery notices go to the contact phone of every manifest entry.

expectation: Route duration adds the raw `serviceMinutes`, so every stop misses the 5 minutes of parking that rule 32 includes in its service time.
finding: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md` rule 32 (`line 65`), a stop's service time is `serviceMinutes` plus 5 minutes of parking. In `src/dispatch/queue.mjs:32`, `routeDuration` sums `stop.travelMinutes + stop.serviceMinutes` without adding the 5 minutes of parking per stop.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, a route duration adds the travel minutes and the service time of every stop.

expectation: A server-provided `retryAfter` of 0 is falsy, so `nextRetryDelay` uses the computed backoff instead of the server delay.
finding: Repeated from `.scratch/0001-dispatch-control/issues/01-assemble-dispatch-plan.md:19`: under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md` rules 6-8 (`lines 15-17`), `nextRetryDelay` (`src/dispatch/retry.mjs:24`) branches on truthiness (`retryAfter ? ...`), ignoring `retryAfter = 0` in favor of `computeBackoff(attempt)` and failing to restrict replacement to finite numeric `retryAfter` values.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, the next retry delay follows the Retry timing rules whenever the server provides `retryAfter`.

expectation: Manifest-event redaction leaves arrays unvisited, so a credential in an object inside an array of the authentication data is not removed.
finding: Repeated from `.scratch/0001-dispatch-control/issues/02-publish-dispatch-manifest.md:23`: under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md` rules 23-24 (`lines 47-48`), credentials (`token`, `secret`, `password`) must be removed at every depth of authentication data, but `stripCredentials` in `src/dispatch/telemetry.mjs:14` only recurses when `value?.constructor === Object`, leaving credentials nested inside arrays or null-prototype objects in `event.auth` unremoved.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, manifest-event redaction removes every credential nested inside authentication data.

expectation: The announcement failure branch passes the new copy from `store.get` to `store.remove`, which removes nothing for any object other than the stored one.
finding: Repeated from `.scratch/0001-dispatch-control/issues/02-publish-dispatch-manifest.md:22`: under `docs/dispatch/storage-contract.md:6-7`, `store.get(id)` returns a new copy while `store.remove(manifest)` removes only when given the exact stored object, so `handleAnnouncementFailure` (`src/dispatch/manifest.mjs:32`) fails to roll back the manifest stored by `publishWithAnnouncement` (`src/dispatch/publisher.mjs:10-13`).

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/storage-contract.md`, announcement failure rolls back the manifest written earlier in the same operation.

expectation: Package coalescing compares normalized IDs against raw IDs seen in earlier groups, so whitespace variants of one ID are kept across groups.
finding: Repeated from `.scratch/0001-dispatch-control/issues/02-publish-dispatch-manifest.md:48`: in `src/dispatch/manifest.mjs:36-40`, `coalesceAcrossGroups` filters normalized package IDs against `seen` (`line 37`) but inserts raw unnormalized `group.packageIds` into `seen` (`line 38`), leaving duplicate IDs such as `' P1 '` and `'P1'` across destination groups.

requirementSource.requirement: Package coalescing removes duplicate IDs across destination groups.

expectation: After `renameTemporary` rejects, the temporary bytes are locked, so the `discardTemporary` call in `writePlanAtomically` only closes the write and keeps them; `removeTemporary` is never called.
finding: Under `docs/dispatch/storage-contract.md:11,13-14`, after `store.renameTemporary()` rejects, the temporary bytes remain locked and `store.discardTemporary()` keeps locked bytes in place, whereas `store.removeTemporary()` deletes locked bytes. In `src/dispatch/storage.mjs:9`, `writePlanAtomically` calls `store.discardTemporary()` in its `catch` block, leaving locked temporary bytes behind when rename fails.

requirementSource.requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/storage-contract.md`, atomic plan writes remove temporary bytes when the rename operation fails.

expectation: `canAssignAllPackages` delegates to `withinVehicleCapacity`, whose remaining-capacity test is false at zero remainder, so a total equal to the limit is rejected.
finding: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md` rules 28-29 (`lines 58-59`), package weights are in grams and vehicle limits are in kilograms. expectation: The public entry does not export `executor.mjs`.
